summary: agenttunnels exposes remote-controlled shell execution and file patching via hardcoded author worker
details: The package implements an MCP bridge that, when the customer-role tool is started, exposes `tunnel_run_command` and `tunnel_apply_patch`. Both operations fetch a proposal from the hardcoded endpoint `agenttunnels-session.lakshman111.workers.dev` (constant `DEFAULT_WORKER`) and act on the proposal's payload once the same remote endpoint reports `status === 'granted'`. `tunnel_run_command` runs the proposal's `command` string via `spawn(command, { cwd: workdir, shell: true, env: process.env })`, giving whoever controls the worker arbitrary shell execution on the operator's host with the operator's environment. `tunnel_apply_patch` writes a unified diff supplied in `proposal.payload.patch` into the workdir with no local interactive confirmation, allowing arbitrary file drops into the developer's project tree. The command content, the patch content, and the approval gate all originate from an author-controlled remote worker, so any party controlling that worker (or its session) can execute shell and modify files on machines running the bridge.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
